title: SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD
status_notes: Issue 5.1 of 26/10/2001 (cover and change log, pp. 1-3). Superseded by issue 5.2 (2/07/03) and the 6.x and 7.0 issues, as recorded in the change logs of later issues (e.g. icd-6-7-drafta, p. 4). Herschel/Planck documents in the library cite it as applicable (H-P-1-ASP-TN-1060 AD2).
summary:
Issue 5.1 (October 2001) of ESOC's SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD, the specification of the Mission Information Base (MIB) as a set of tab-separated ASCII tables that a mission's off-line database exports and the SCOS-2000 importer loads into its run-time database. This copy comes from the Herschel SPIRE archive, where it was an applicable document for the SCOS-2000-based instrument EGSE. Its change log describes it as covering SCOS-2000 R2.3 (to be implemented in R3.0) plus specific additions for EGSE systems.

Chapter 2 fixes the file conventions: one `<table>.dat` file per table, one file per OL synthetic parameter, tab separators, the import-time checks with their fallback values, and the import options. Chapter 3 first maps database items to tables, then summarises 46 tables and defines every field (position, name, type, length, mandatory flag or default). The tables cover monitoring (pcf, caf/cap, txf/txp, mcf, ocf/ocp, pid, pic, tpcf, plf, vpd), displays (dpf/dpc, gpf/gpc, spf/spc, ppf/ppc) and commanding: packet headers (tcp, pcpc, pcdf), commands (ccf, the EGSE-only routing table dst, cpc, cdf, ptv), sequences (csf, css, sdf, csp), verification (cvs, cve, cvp), parameter sets (pst, psv, cps, pvs, psm), de-calibrations (cca/ccs, paf/pas) and range checks (prf/prv).

Appendix A gives the PTC/PFC parameter type codes SCOS-2000 supports, mapped to the ESA PUS (PSS-07-101), with raw value formats. Appendix B draws the table relationships, and Annex 1 lists the DCRs implemented since issue 4.x. Read it alongside later issues to see how the MIB evolved: here curve identifiers are still 4-digit numbers, descriptions are 16 characters, and there are no conditional calibrations, logarithmic curves or groups.

key_points.text: The ICD covers only the 'generic' part of the static database relevant to SCOS-2000 functions; mission-specific extensions are possible. MIB data are exported from the off-line database (e.g. ORACLE, MS-Access) into ASCII files, transferred to the importer directory, imported, and used when applications restart.

The SCOS-2000 Mission Information Base is split into a static part (the 'database') and a dynamic part (the 'history files'). The raw value differs from the encoded value except for unsigned integers; e.g. raw -1 of a 16-bit signed integer is encoded as FFFF hex.

Each table is one ASCII file named after the table in lower case with extension .dat (e.g. pcf.dat); each dynamic OL synthetic parameter is a separate file named after its PCF_NAME, without extension, in a dedicated sub-directory. Fields are tab-separated and mission-specific fields are appended at the end of a record.

Import-time checks truncate over-long fields with a warning, replace null mandatory fields with 0 or an empty string, drop records that break relational integrity, and reset invalid command parameter values to 0, "" or 1970.001.00.00.00; messages go to /home/sops1/Import.log.
Import options are full import (default), monitoring tables only, commanding tables only, selected tables only, and 'check only'.

Key fields are marked with '*' after the field position; grey rows are not used by SCOS-2000; italics mark options not yet supported; 'M' marks mandatory fields; name uniqueness is case-insensitive (A1000 and a1000 clash).
Section 3.2 summarises 46 ASCII tables: vdf; 13 monitoring tables; 6 display tables; and 26 commanding tables including the new dst routing table.
The VDF table is mandatory; if it holds several records the last imported one defines the database version name (VDF_NAME, Char(8)).

PCF is the central monitoring table. PCF_NAME is Char(8) and may not start with 'VAR', 'GVAR' or '$' (reserved by the OL syntax); PCF_DESCR is Char(16); PCF_PID (Number(10)) links a parameter to its on-board parameter ID for PUS variable packets.
PCF_PTC takes values 1 to 13; saved synthetic parameters (PCF_NATUR='S') must use PTC=13. The PCF table has 19 fields in this issue.

A TM packet is identified by the PID key TYPE, STYPE, APID, PI1_VAL and PI2_VAL; several keys may map to one SPID, and PID_VALID selects among records with the same key. The APID/type/subtype-to-SPID allocation should not change once telemetry archiving starts, for the GDDS retrieval services.

The optional DST table (EGSE systems only) gives, per APID, a destination ID of up to 3 dot-separated fields ('NCTRS' by default, or 'EGSE' for spacecraft and non-spacecraft commands, e.g. 'EGSE.TC.0x8800').
Command parameter calibration and range-set references (CPC_PRFREF, CPC_CCAREF, CPC_PAFREF) are Number(4) in this issue.
Appendix A maps SCOS-2000 PTC/PFC pairs to the PUS; 48- and 64-bit integers (PTC 3/4, PFC 15/16) are not supported.

PTC=5 PFC=3 is a 32-bit MIL-STD-1750A real (normally called PTC=5, PFC=2 in ESA missions) and PTC=5 PFC=4 a 48-bit MIL-STD-1750A real; PTC=6 PFC>0 bit strings are treated as unsigned integers on the monitoring side only.
PTC=11 denotes deduced parameters and PTC=13 saved synthetic parameters.
Absolute times are entered as yyyy.ddd.hh.mm.ss (e.g. 2001.159.23.59.59) and relative times as +/-[ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm]; neither can be associated with a calibration curve.

DCR-266 (EGSE) widens CCF_APID, CCF_RAPID and PID_APID from num(4) to num(5): 0 to 2047 identify on-board APIDs and 2048 to 65535 ground process IDs. DCR-241 adds a command category (CCF_TYPE='S') for which the Releaser appends no CRC.

notes: This copy comes from the Herschel SPIRE document archive: the cover carries the stamp SPIRE-ESA-DOC-002339, and the file name labels it 'AD11 - s2k-mcs-icd-0001-tos-gci_51'. Printed page 1 is PDF page 9 (offset +8). The copyright line reads 1998. The text extraction inserts spaces into document numbers (e.g. 'S2K-MCS -SRD-0003-TOS-GCI' and the running header 'S2K-MCS -ICD-0001-TOS-GCI'); these are normalised here to the cover form without spaces. RD-14 is printed 'ESA PSS-074-107' (the ESA Packet Telecommand Standard is usually numbered PSS-04-107). The table of contents lists 'Annex 1 – List of implemented Document Changes' twice. The PID table numbers both PID_EVENT and PID_EVID as field 15 (p. 42). The 3.2 summary omits the ppf/ppc printout tables, which are nevertheless defined in sections 3.3.2.6.7-8. Appendix B figures are diagrams; their extracted text is fragmentary. Related library items: later issues icd-6-7-drafta, icd-6-9-archive-org and icd-7-0-final; Herschel tailoring documents h-p-1-asp-tn-1060-mib-processing-hpsdb (which cites this issue as AD2) and hcss-mib-clarification-tailoring-note (which cites issue 5.2). RD-8 CCSDS 301.0-B-2 is an older issue of library item ccsds-301-0-301x0b4e1.
